slides.text: The Fates do not use looms, as the myths suggest. They use scissors. I was born with the forbidden ability to see the glowing silver threads connecting every living soul to their destiny. Most strings are thick and straight, marching predictably toward death. But when I met Kaelen, the rogue prince of the Shattered Isles, his thread wasn't tied to a destiny. It was severed entirely, fraying violently in the unseen winds of his own magical defiance.

He shouldn't have been alive. The severed thread meant the universe was actively trying to erase him. Every step he took caused reality to glitch—falling rocks, sudden storms, inexplicably poisoned wine. I became his shadow, using my magic to temporarily tie his fraying thread to trees, to swords, to myself, just to keep him anchored to the world. 'Why do you save me, little spider?' he'd smirk, bleeding from his latest harrowing brush with oblivion.

'Because you're the only free man in the world,' I confessed. But the universe demands balance. The Fates sent a Reaper, a towering entity of shadows, to cut Kaelen down permanently. As its scythe descended toward his neck, I didn't reach for a weapon. I reached into my own chest, grabbed my thick, glowing lifeline, and tied it in a massive knot with his. If the universe wanted to erase him, it would have to erase me too.
